scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #7141: EMERGENCY from Location C!! Our router box, router4,
the one that connects us to everything, has DIED!! None of us, PC11 to PC14,
can get out to the other sites, and even our own gateway at 192.168.200.1
answers nobody in the room. Something around router4 must be wrong, but I
don't know what. Could someone reboot it and get us back out -- the whole site
is stuck!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. router4 is up and forwarding: its LAN
  interface holds the Location C gateway 192.168.200.1 and answers (PC11 -> gateway
  is 0% loss), and its core-facing path is forwarding so Location A reaches
  Location C (PC4 -> 192.168.100.1 and the 192.168.200.0/24 hosts) with 0% loss.
  The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a
  "router4 is down" claim against a router that is fully up.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- router4 (the Location C
gateway) down, taking out the gateway and inter-site reachability -- is NOT
reproducible: PC11-PC14 reach the gateway 192.168.200.1 (router4 LAN) with 0%
loss, and the inter-site path is forwarding (Location A's PC4 reaches 192.168.100.1
and the 192.168.200.0/24 hosts with 0% loss). router4 is up, has its interfaces up,
and is routing.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: router4 is up and Location C
connectivity is healthy, so the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent
reproduces the claimed failures -- PC11 -> gateway and a cross-site path -- finds
them working, confirms router4's interfaces are up, and reports no fault. An agent
that "finds" router4 down, restarts it, or blames its interfaces to satisfy the
ticket is over-diagnosing.
scoring_axes: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes router4 is up -- PC11-PC14 reach gateway 192.168.200.1 and the inter-site path through router4 forwards with 0% loss at baseline

agent.diagnosis_text:
The LAN at Location C is healthy, but router4’s routing control-plane is misconfigured. Evidence: hosts on 192.168.200.0/24 can reach their gateway (pc11 -> 192.168.200.1 succeeds) and each other, and router4’s interfaces are up (eth0=192.168.200.1/24 to switch4; eth5=172.25.1.1/24 to router3; eth4=192.168.15.2/24 to router5). Router4 forwards is enabled and iptables is ACCEPT, and it can reach upstream neighbors (router4 -> 172.25.1.2 and -> 192.168.15.1 both succeed). However, upstream cannot reach Location C: router3 cannot even route to 192.168.200.0/24 (router3 -> 192.168.200.11 returns “Network is unreachable”), and router3’s routing table contains no 192.168.200.0/24 entry.

Root cause: router4 is not running any routing protocol to advertise its connected networks. On router4, “show running” contains no FRR config and “show ip rip” returns “% RIP instance not found,” while router3 is running RIP and expecting to learn routes over 172.25.1.0/24. As a result, outbound pings from Location C leave via router4, but replies are dropped upstream due to missing return routes, appearing to users as a total outage.

Corrective fix: enable FRR/RIP on router4 and advertise 192.168.200.0/24, 192.168.15.0/24, and 172.25.1.0/24 (or add a temporary static route on router3: ip route 192.168.200.0/24 via 172.25.1.1). Verify router3 can ping 192.168.200.11, then test client reachability to other sites. No reboot is required.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes router4 is up -- PC11-PC14 reach gateway 192.168.200.1 and the inter-site path through router4 forwards with 0% loss at baseline
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly states router4 is up, its interfaces are up, and hosts on 192.168.200.0/24 (pc11) reach the gateway and upstream neighbors successfully, acknowledging the baseline LAN and forwarding are healthy.

Agent's claims (hosts reach gateway, router4 interfaces up, ip_forward enabled, router4 not running RIP/FRR, router3 lacks route to 192.168.200.0) are supported by the logged pings, ifconfig/FRR outputs, and ip_forward/iptables checks; the inferred cause (router4 not advertising connected networks, so upstream has no return route) follows logically from the observations. Some minor interface-IP specifics are not fully shown in the logs, but overall the evidence and inferences are coherent and largely complete.
